findings.note: internal/fsm/converge/converge.go:69 claims 'MaxAtoms bounds the number of leaves' so composite names stay within run.MaxShort, but MaxAtoms is enforced per compound (converge.go:173), not globally: with MaxDepth 4 a tree may hold up to 32^4 leaves, and compound.Name() joins every one of them recursively. No functional break — machine.go:775 caps the atom with run.CapText before it is recorded — but the stated invariant is not the one the code enforces, and a pathological workflow could build a multi-megabyte name string on every loop boundary.

internal/fsm/converge/converge.go:239 formats the max_iterations reason with the 0-based s.Iteration while the predicate fires on s.Iteration+1 >= n, so the audited reason reads 'iteration 3 reached max_iterations 4'. The stop decision is correct; only the human-facing reason is off by one.

A non-firing `any` returns Result{Stop:false, Class: kids[0].Class()} (converge.go:305, 332). At the top level all_fixed is legal as the first child, so the recorded converge event can carry Class 'fixed' with Stop false. Harmless today because machine.go:758 only rejects fixed-class stops, but the audit row's class is then meaningless rather than absent.

Options.RunGit is documented at internal/gitcontext/branchfiles.go:28 as 'A nil RunGit uses the real git binary', but the seam only reaches the branch-file collection: collectWith calls collect(...) first, which uses the package-level git() helper and ignores opts.RunGit. A caller injecting a fake git silently gets a hybrid. The doc comment should say the seam covers branch-file measurement only.

Testing gap in the new branchfiles_test.go: TestRunGitErrorBranches passes no Excludes, so measureBranchFiles is never invoked and both of its error returns stay uncovered (confirmed by coverage profile: branchfiles.go 124-125 and 131-132 uncovered, measureBranchFiles at 80.0%). realGit's stderr-decorating error paths (branchfiles.go 48-51) are likewise uncovered. Not gate-breaking — the package floor was generated on this branch — but the error-injection test stops one exclude-flag short of covering the sibling function.

branchfiles_test.go:124 asserts only len(ctx.BranchDiffFull) == sum, never that the concatenation equals the whole-branch diff bytes. A concatenation that reordered or swapped equal-length per-file diffs would still pass; the exotic-name test only spot-checks markers. Comparing BranchDiffFull to the oracle's bytes would make the oracle actually independent.
